chunks: A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) enter the Sacred Masjid during the Asr prayer. When the congregation was bowing (in Ruku'), he bowed alone, then prostrated two prostrations, then stood up and continued until he joined the rows.
ai.seo_question: How should a person pray if they arrive late to the congregational prayer and miss the Imam's bowing?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of *Qada'* (making up missed units) for a latecomer who arrives after the Imam has already bowed. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the latecomer completes the missed *Ruku'* individually before joining the Imam for the remaining units, ensuring the validity of their prayer despite the delay. This incident serves as a foundational precedent for the jurisprudence of *Salat al-Muqtadi* (prayer of the follower) in Shia fiqh.
